episodes.188068: A strong system approached the region for the start of March, with very anomalously strong low level flow noted ahead of a cold frontal boundary. This strong low level flow resulted in a prolonged period of strong sustained and gusty winds across almost the entirety of Utah. As the cold front moved into northern Utah, some areas experienced  convective precipitation and associated strong wind gusts. Winds began to subside following the passage of the cold front, but the colder air allowed for precipitation to transition to snow, yielding accumulating snow across much of the area. Mountain locations which remained sufficiently cold throughout the event received fairly substantial snow accumulations in addition to the prolonged strong winds.
episodes.188186: A cold front moved through central California on March 1 and 2, with gusty winds and scattered thunderstorms. Radar indicated rotation in Monterey Bay would result in the first Tornado Warnings issued by the Monterey/San Francisco Bay Area office since March 2011. No damage was noted in a subsequent survey.
episodes.189522: Strong Winds and Widespread Precipitation Impact Southern California on March 2. The strongest winds were reported in the mountains and along the desert slopes, where gusts over 70 mph occurred. Widely beneficial precipitation fell, but reports of flooding were received in the San Bernardino County Mountains.
episodes.189951: A few thunderstorms occurred across southwest Georgia with one storm producing penny sized hail in Thomas county.
episodes.190495: A storm system brought convective storms to the coastal waters with strong winds and waterspouts.
episodes.190496: A deep trough brought widespread hail showers and snow to Northwest California. Heavy snow of several feet was measured in the mountains while the hail showers resulted in numerous traffic accidents along the coast.

Heavy rain fell across Orange County, mainly during the day on March 2. Santiago Peak reported rainfall of 4.41, with Upper Harding Cyn seeing 3.19. Most areas in the Santa Ana Mountains saw 0.75-2.5. The coast and valleys in Orange County saw anywhere from 0.25-0.90.

Heavy precipitation fell across San Bernardino County on March 2. Most mountain locations saw 1.00-3.00, though some locations saw over 5 inches of rain. Lower elevations in the Inland Empire saw 0.50-2.00.

Heavy rain fell across Riverside County on March 2. The mountains saw accumulations of 0.50-1.80, while lower elevations in the Inland Empire saw 0.20-0.80. The lower deserts saw minimal accumulations.

Heavy rain fell across San Diego County on March 2. The mountains saw accumulations of 0.50-2.50, while lower elevations across the coast and valleys saw 0.25-1.00, with locally higher amounts. The lower deserts saw minimal accumulations.
